note: One source is committed as bytes and one is not. The Regulation is the measured object: every number in this work is derived from the committed HTML by measure.py, and EUR-Lex's own legal notice says the legal documents published there may be re-used for commercial or non-commercial purposes under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, so the bytes are here and the night is re-runnable without a network. The drafting guide is a citation, not a population -- it is quoted within citation length and identified by hash. Both files were fetched twice on the night and the Regulation returned byte-identical content both times, which is recorded because a manifest hash is worthless against a source that changes between fetches.

sources.what: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation), English, as published by EUR-Lex -- THE POPULATION
sources.why: the object: 173 recitals with no binding force and 99 articles with it, in one file, marked up by EUR-Lex with the ELI subdivision anchors rct_1..173 and art_1..99 that measure.py cuts on
sources.licence: EUR-Lex legal notice, reuse policy based on Commission Decision 2011/833/EU: 'Unless otherwise specified, you can re-use the legal documents published in EUR-Lex for commercial or non-commercial purposes.' (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/content/legal-notice/legal-notice.html)

sources.what: Joint Practical Guide of the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission for persons involved in the drafting of European Union legislation -- THE NORM THE POPULATION IS HELD TO
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union, Luxembourg, 2015
sources.why: Guideline 10 states the rule this measurement counts violations of. Quoted in work.md within citation length; not committed, because nothing here is derived from it computationally.
sources.licence: '(c) European Union, 2015. Reproduction is authorised provided the source is acknowledged.' -- redistribution would be lawful; the manifest is the better warrant and the file is not the measured object.
sources.read: in full text, extracted locally from the PDF; the passages used are Guideline 10's heading, 10.1, 10.5.1-10.5.2, and the foreword's statement of the guide's own basis in the Interinstitutional Agreement of 22 December 1998 (OJ C 73, 17.3.1999, p. 1)

sources.what: Judgment of the Court (First Chamber), 27 February 2025, C-203/22, CK v Dun & Bradstreet Austria GmbH
sources.why: the ruling that made recital 71's explanation enforceable through Article 15(1)(h). Read in Session 80 (journal/2026-09-04.md), where paragraphs 55 and 57 and the operative part are quoted; cited here, not re-derived.

sources.what: Judgment of the Court, 19 November 1998, C-162/97, Nilsson and others
sources.why: paragraph 54: 'the preamble to a Community act has no binding legal force'. This is the premise that makes the preamble the non-binding half. Read in Session 80; cited here.
